key_insight: Graphene oxide changes the temperature dependence of heat transport in epoxy composites rather than simply enhancing thermal conductivity.
engineering_relevance: Thermal design with epoxy–graphene oxide composites should account for filler loading and operating temperature across cryogenic-to-ambient conditions.
method: Studied nominal GO loadings of 0.25–10 wt.% relative to resin.
Characterized structure using X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy.
Measured thermal conductivity from 4.5–300 K and fitted a phenomenological multichannel model.
evidence_signal: X-ray diffraction showed no detectable GO(001) reflection, while the low-temperature conductivity plateau resolved at lower GO loadings was no longer resolved in GO-6 and GO-10.
watch_item: The fitted transport channels are phenomenological and do not establish unique microscopic heat-transfer mechanisms.
paper_title: Structure and Thermal Conductivity of Epoxy-Graphene Oxide Composites from 4.5 to 300 K
